function: LSTM predicts next UAV position and AIRS phase-shift vector for RSMA user groups to raise sum-rate; BS precoder by non-learned alternating optimization (pp. 1, 7-8).
system: Downlink MISO-RSMA: BS with 4 antennas, 2 groups of 3 single-antenna users, UAV-mounted reflecting IRS with 60 elements, 2-bit phases; band not stated (pp. 3-4, 8).
method: Two LSTM models (trajectory: one layer; phase shift: two layers), supervised MSE regression with Adam, trained on static, dynamic, and combined user data (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Own simulation: Nakagami small-scale fading, distance-based path loss; training data generated by the authors' search policy over UAV positions and phase vectors (pp. 3-4, 7-9).
test_conditions: Trained at SNR 40 dB, tested at SNR 10-40 dB and SIC error 0.01/0.1 (p. 11); models tested in scenarios whose data they were trained on (pp. 10-11).
baselines: Random (non-optimized) precoder, AIRS-NOMA, GRU with the same observation space; static, dynamic, and combined LSTM variants (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Sum-rate versus episodes and SNR, group achievable rate and fairness, RMSE and training loss, UAV trajectory (pp. 9-11).
complexity: About 5 million parameters for the phase-shift LSTM, trajectory LSTM almost 5 times smaller (p. 9); order of the non-learned AO beamformer in Eq. 31 (p. 6).
q1_support: p. 3: "denote the small-scale fading, modeled by the Nakagami distribution, as in [12]". Custom model with distance-based path loss; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "Fig. 9 investigates the total sum-rate for the static scenario versus the transmit SNR". Models are trained at 40 dB (p. 11), so this is an SNR sweep; the combined dyn-sta model is trained on both static and dynamic data, and no model is tested in a scenario absent from its training data.
q3_support: p. 10: "The analysis considers both non-optimized, where a random precoder is used, and optimized beamforming approaches". The random precoder concerns BS beamforming, not the learned UAV trajectory or phase shift; the only learned comparator is GRU (p. 11, Figs. 11-12); no non-learned baseline for trajectory or phase shift is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "the second model has approximately 5 million parameters to optimize, while the first is almost 5 times smaller". Tables I and II (pp. 7-8) list layer sizes of the two LSTM models.
q5_support: p. 7: "The model was implemented using Matlab with Deep Learning Tool Box associated". No code or data link; training data come from the authors' own simulation (p. 9).
notes: Included, area 6: UAV-mounted RIS (aerial link); the LSTM predicts UAV trajectory (above PHY) jointly with RIS phase shifts (PHY), so it passes above_phy; BS beamforming is non-learned AO. Reviewer may reassign to area 3 (RIS phase shifts). q3 is 0: only GRU is a learned comparator, and the random precoder concerns BS beamforming, not the learned functions. q4 relies on the stated parameter counts. Carrier frequency is not stated.
